category: Visual LISP String, List, File & Registry Functions (vl-)
description: The vl- extension functions that fill the gaps of classic AutoLISP: string search, trimming and substitution; character-code conversion; higher-order list functions (remove-if, some, every, position); file and directory handling; file-name parsing; Windows registry access; symbol utilities; VBA loading and FAS compilation. Most work without (vl-load-com) and are available in AutoCAD LT 2024+ and AutoCAD for Mac unless noted.

tools.name: vl-string-subst
tools.description: Substitutes the first occurrence of a pattern string within a string with a new string, optionally starting at a given position. It replaces only one occurrence per call, so a loop is needed for replace-all behaviour.
tools.example:
(defun replace-all (new old str / p)
  (setq p 0)
  (while (setq p (vl-string-search old str p))
    (setq str (vl-string-subst new old str p)
          p   (+ p (strlen new))))
  str)
(replace-all "-" "_" "A_B_C") ; -> "A-B-C"
tools.notes: Case-sensitive; use strcase on both strings for case-insensitive matching. Returns the original string unchanged when the pattern is not found.

tools.name: vl-string-trim
tools.description: Removes any of a set of characters from both the beginning and the end of a string. Commonly used to strip spaces, tabs and newlines from text read from files or attributes.

parameters.name: chars-set
parameters.description: String listing the characters to remove, e.g. " \t\n".

tools.notes: chars-set is a set of single characters, not a substring. Use vl-string-left-trim or vl-string-right-trim to trim one side only.

tools.name: vl-string-left-trim
tools.description: Removes any of the specified characters from the beginning of a string only. Useful for stripping leading zeros or prefixes made of repeated characters.
tools.notes: A string consisting only of trim characters returns "".

tools.name: vl-string-right-trim
tools.description: Removes any of the specified characters from the end of a string. Often used to remove trailing zeros from numbers formatted with rtos or trailing path separators.
tools.notes: DIMZIN also controls trailing zeros for rtos output, but trimming is locale- and setting-independent.

tools.name: vl-string-translate
tools.description: Replaces characters in a string character-by-character according to a source set and a destination set, like the Unix tr command. Useful for normalizing path separators or replacing illegal characters in layer or file names.

parameters.name: dest-set
parameters.description: Replacement characters at the same positions.

tools.notes: Each character of str found in source-set is replaced by the character at the same position in dest-set; keep both sets the same length. For multi-character substitutions use vl-string-subst.

tools.name: vl-string-position
tools.description: Returns the zero-based index of a character (given by its ASCII code) in a string, searching forward or from the end. It is the fastest way to split on a delimiter or find the last path separator.

parameters.name: char-code
parameters.description: Integer character code, e.g. 44 for comma or (ascii ",").

parameters.name: start-pos
parameters.description: Index to start searching from; nil for default.

parameters.name: from-end-p
parameters.description: T to search backwards from the end.

tools.example:
(defun split (str ch / p lst)
  (while (setq p (vl-string-position (ascii ch) str))
    (setq lst (cons (substr str 1 p) lst) str (substr str (+ p 2))))
  (reverse (cons str lst)))
(split "A,B,C" ",") ; -> ("A" "B" "C")
tools.notes: Positions are zero-based while substr is one-based; add 1 when converting. Returns nil if the character is absent.

tools.name: vl-string-mismatch
tools.description: Returns the length of the longest common prefix of two strings, optionally starting at given positions and ignoring case. Useful for sorting or grouping names that share a prefix such as layer name families.
tools.notes: Returns 0 when the first characters differ.

tools.name: vl-string->list
tools.description: Converts a string into a list of its character codes. Combined with list functions and vl-list->string it allows character-level processing such as filtering digits or reversing text.
tools.notes: Codes depend on the drawing code page for non-ASCII characters; Unicode text uses \U+XXXX sequences in some contexts.

tools.name: vl-list->string
tools.description: Combines a list of character codes into a string, the inverse of vl-string->list.
tools.notes: An empty list returns "".

tools.name: vl-string-elt
tools.description: Returns the character code at a zero-based position in a string. It is cheaper than (ascii (substr str (1+ i) 1)) inside loops.
tools.notes: Raises an error when the index is out of range.

tools.name: vl-prin1-to-string
tools.description: Returns the printed representation of any LISP value as prin1 would output it, with strings quoted and escape characters shown. Useful for writing data to files so that it can be read back with read.
tools.notes: Round-trips through read for lists, numbers and strings, but not for entity names, selection sets or VLA-objects.

tools.name: vl-princ-to-string
tools.description: Returns the representation of a LISP value as princ would display it, without quotes around strings. The quick way to turn numbers, points or symbols into readable text for prompts and reports.
tools.notes: Reals are shown with the default LUPREC-independent formatting; use rtos for controlled precision.

tools.name: vl-position
tools.description: Returns the zero-based index of an item in a list, comparing with equal. Returns nil when the item is not found.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: Item to look for (any LISP value).

tools.notes: Often used with DCL popup lists, whose values are indexes into a list.

tools.name: vl-remove-if
tools.description: Returns a copy of a list without the elements for which a predicate function returns true. It is the functional filter used to discard unwanted items such as nil entries or objects on frozen layers.

parameters.name: predicate-function
parameters.description: Quoted function or lambda of one argument.

tools.notes: Non-destructive: the original list is unchanged.

tools.name: vl-remove-if-not
tools.description: Returns only the elements of a list for which a predicate returns true, the positive filter complementing vl-remove-if.

parameters.name: predicate-function
parameters.description: Quoted function or lambda of one argument.

tools.notes: For finding just the first match, vl-member-if is faster because it stops early.

tools.name: vl-member-if-not
tools.description: Returns the tail of a list starting at the first element for which the predicate returns nil, or nil if the predicate is true for all elements.

parameters.name: predicate-function
parameters.description: Quoted function or lambda of one argument.

tools.notes: Complement of vl-member-if.

tools.name: vl-some
tools.description: Applies a predicate to successive elements of one or more lists and returns the first non-nil result, or nil if none. Equivalent to 'any' in other languages and stops at the first success.

parameters.name: predicate-function
parameters.description: Function taking as many arguments as lists supplied.

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: One or more lists processed in parallel.

tools.example:
(vl-some '(lambda (f) (findfile f)) '("std.dwt" "acadiso.dwt" "acad.dwt"))
; -> full path of the first template found
tools.notes: Returns the predicate's value, not the element, which makes it handy for 'find first existing' patterns.

tools.name: vl-every
tools.description: Returns T if a predicate is true for every element (or every parallel combination of elements) of the supplied lists, nil as soon as one fails.

parameters.name: predicate-function
parameters.description: Function taking as many arguments as lists supplied.

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Lists processed in parallel; stops at the shortest.

tools.notes: Returns T for empty lists.

tools.name: vl-list*
tools.description: Constructs a list like list, but uses the last argument as the tail, so the result can be a dotted pair or a list prepended to an existing list. Frequently used to build DXF-style dotted pairs with computed values.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: Elements; the final one becomes the cdr of the last cons.

tools.notes: (vl-list* a b) is equivalent to (cons a b).

tools.name: vl-list-length
tools.description: Returns the length of a true list, or nil if the argument is a dotted list. Safer than length when data may contain dotted pairs.
tools.notes: length raises an error on dotted pairs; vl-list-length does not.

tools.name: vl-consp
tools.description: Returns T if the argument is a non-empty list (a cons cell), nil otherwise. Unlike listp, it is false for nil, which makes it a precise test for 'has data'.
tools.notes: (listp nil) is T but (vl-consp nil) is nil.

tools.name: vl-sort-i
tools.description: Sorts a list with a comparison function but returns the list of original indexes in sorted order rather than the sorted elements. Unlike vl-sort, it keeps duplicates, and the indexes can reorder parallel lists.

parameters.name: comparison-function
parameters.description: Function of two arguments returning true when the first should come first, e.g. '< or '>.

tools.notes: vl-sort removes duplicate numbers in some cases; vl-sort-i never drops elements.

tools.name: vl-symbol-value
tools.description: Returns the current value bound to a symbol, like eval on a quoted symbol but without evaluating it as an expression. Useful for reading variables whose names are constructed at run time.

parameters.name: symbol
parameters.description: A symbol (usually from read or vl-symbol-name manipulation).

tools.notes: Related: vl-symbolp tests whether an object is a symbol; vl-symbol-name returns its name.

tools.name: vl-catch-all-error-message
tools.description: Returns the error message string from an error object produced by vl-catch-all-apply. Used to report or log what went wrong without aborting the routine.

parameters.name: error-obj
parameters.description: Object returned by vl-catch-all-apply when vl-catch-all-error-p is true.

tools.notes: ActiveX errors produce messages beginning 'Automation Error.' followed by the server message.

tools.name: vl-file-copy
tools.description: Copies a file to a new location, or appends its contents to an existing file when the append flag is set. Returns the number of bytes copied, or nil on failure (for example when the destination exists and append is not set).

parameters.name: source-file
parameters.description: Path of the file to copy.

parameters.name: append
parameters.description: T to append to an existing destination.

tools.example:
(if (not (vl-file-copy "P:/Std/titleblock.dwg" "C:/Work/titleblock.dwg"))
  (princ "\nCopy failed - destination exists or path invalid."))
tools.notes: Does not overwrite; delete the destination first with vl-file-delete. Cannot copy a file onto itself or copy open, locked files.

tools.name: vl-file-delete
tools.description: Deletes a file and returns T on success, nil on failure. Frequently used to remove temporary files or an existing target before vl-file-copy.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Path of the file; relative names use the current directory.

tools.notes: The file is removed permanently (not moved to the Recycle Bin).

tools.name: vl-file-rename
tools.description: Renames or moves a file. Returns T on success, nil if the source does not exist or the target already exists.
tools.notes: Moving across drives works like a copy plus delete; the target must not exist.

tools.name: vl-file-directory-p
tools.description: Returns T if a path refers to an existing directory, nil otherwise. Used to validate output folders before writing and to decide whether to create them with vl-mkdir.
tools.notes: findfile also finds directories, but vl-file-directory-p distinguishes them from files.

tools.name: vl-file-size
tools.description: Returns the size of a file in bytes, 0 for a directory, or nil if the file does not exist.
tools.notes: Handy to detect empty exports or truncated files.

tools.name: vl-file-systime
tools.description: Returns the last-modification time of a file as a list (year month day-of-week day hours minutes seconds milliseconds). Used to compare timestamps, for example to rebuild an export only when the drawing is newer.
tools.notes: Day-of-week is 0 for Sunday. Returns nil for missing files.

tools.name: vl-filename-base
tools.description: Returns a file name without its directory path and extension. Standard building block for naming exports after the drawing.
tools.notes: Does not check that the file exists.

tools.name: vl-filename-directory
tools.description: Returns the directory part of a file path, without the trailing separator.
tools.notes: Returns "" when the argument contains no directory.

tools.name: vl-filename-extension
tools.description: Returns the extension of a file name including the leading period, or nil when there is none.
tools.notes: Compare in a case-insensitive way; Windows file names are not case-sensitive.

tools.name: vl-filename-mktemp
tools.description: Returns a unique file name suitable for a temporary file, built from an optional pattern, directory and extension. By default it uses the TEMP folder.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Base name pattern; a unique suffix is appended.

parameters.name: directory
parameters.description: Folder; defaults to the system temporary directory.

tools.example:
(setq scr (vl-filename-mktemp "batch" nil ".scr"))
(setq f (open scr "w")) (write-line "_.QSAVE" f) (close f)
tools.notes: The file is not created, only named; open it for writing yourself.

tools.name: vl-directory-files
tools.description: Lists the files and/or subdirectories of a folder that match a wildcard pattern. It is the core of batch-processing routines that iterate drawings in a directory.

parameters.name: directory
parameters.description: Folder to list; nil for the current directory.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Wildcard such as "*.dwg"; nil for all.

parameters.name: directories
parameters.description: -1 directories only, 0 files and directories (default), 1 files only.

tools.example:
(foreach f (vl-directory-files "C:/Proj/Sheets" "*.dwg" 1)
  (princ (strcat "\n" f)))
(vl-directory-files "C:/Proj" nil -1) ; subfolders, includes "." and ".."
tools.notes: Returns names only, not full paths. Subdirectory listings include "." and ".."; filter them out before recursing.

tools.name: vl-mkdir
tools.description: Creates a directory and returns T on success. It creates only one level, so nested paths must be created parent first.

parameters.name: directoryname
parameters.description: Path of the directory to create.

tools.notes: Returns nil if the directory already exists or cannot be created.

tools.name: vl-registry-write
tools.description: Creates a registry key and optionally writes a value to it. Used to store per-user application settings under HKEY_CURRENT_USER. On Mac it writes to a property list file.

parameters.name: val-name
parameters.description: Value name; nil or omitted for the default value.

tools.notes: Writing to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE requires administrator rights. For AutoCAD profile-specific storage, use (vlax-user-product-key) as the base path, or setenv/getenv.

tools.name: vl-registry-delete
tools.description: Deletes a registry value, or a key when no value name is given. Used by uninstall routines to clean up application settings.

parameters.name: val-name
parameters.description: Value to delete; omit to delete the key.

tools.notes: A key that still has subkeys cannot be deleted; remove subkeys first (enumerate with vl-registry-descendents).

tools.name: vl-registry-descendents
tools.description: Returns the list of subkeys of a registry key, or its value names when the second argument is non-nil. Used to enumerate installed profiles, product versions or stored settings.

parameters.name: val-names
parameters.description: Non-nil to return value names instead of subkeys.

tools.notes: Requires (vl-load-com) for vlax-user-product-key in this example.

tools.name: vl-vbarun
tools.description: Runs a VBA macro from AutoLISP, after the project has been loaded with vl-vbaload. It lets LISP menus and scripts call legacy VBA code.

parameters.name: macroname
parameters.description: Macro name, optionally qualified with the project file and module.

tools.notes: Requires the separately downloaded VBA enabler for AutoCAD; not available in AutoCAD LT or on Mac. Macros cannot take arguments; exchange data via system variables such as USERS1-5.

tools.name: vlisp-compile
tools.description: Compiles an AutoLISP source file into a .fas file, protecting the source and speeding up loading. The mode selects standard, optimized with internal links, or optimized with indirect links compilation.

parameters.name: output
parameters.description: Target .fas name; defaults to the source name with .fas.

tools.notes: LISPSYS decides the FAS format: with LISPSYS = 1 (Unicode) the result cannot be loaded in AutoCAD 2020 or earlier, so set 0 or 2 before compiling for older targets. An output name without a path is written to the AutoCAD installation folder, so always give a full path. Use MAKELISPAPP to combine several files and DCL into a .vlx application.
